allObjections.title: Runtime enforcement gap
allObjections.detail: §B.2 validity rules exist only in spec with no implementation. The proposal admits in Conflict 10 that AutoRunner doesn't enforce these rules today, meaning users can submit invalid 324-cell combinations that will fail unpredictably.

allObjections.title: Attestation mechanism is toothless
allObjections.detail: §A.1.4's ownership attestation relies entirely on operator self-declaration with no verification. A malicious operator can simply check 'owned' for any URL and FlowAI will synthesize from competitors' sites, creating legal liability.

allObjections.title: Authority dimension explosion
allObjections.detail: §A.2's split from 1 to 3 authority dimensions creates 3^3=27 authority combinations per mode. Combined with 4 modes and 3 execution modes, operators must reason about 324 theoretical states, even if only ~16 are valid.

allObjections.title: JSONB migration without rollback
allObjections.detail: Conflict 7 proposes adding a JSONB column to ProductRegistry with a complex nested structure but no migration rollback path. If the 4×3 matrix proves unwieldy, reverting requires manual data transformation.

allObjections.title: Mode 3B spec-only output contradicts synthesis
allObjections.detail: §A.1.4 claims Mode 3B produces a 'synthesized product specification' but §D shows it just runs Mode 1 steps 1-4 on each URL then somehow 'extracts best elements' in step 6 with no concrete extraction algorithm specified.

allObjections.title: Lack of Rollback
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not provide a clear rollback strategy in case of errors or issues with the new authority dimensions, which could lead to unintended consequences and make it difficult to revert to a previous state.

allObjections.title: Insufficient Validation
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not specify how the new authority dimensions will be validated, which could lead to inconsistencies and errors in the system. For example, the proposal mentions that the operator sets the ceiling for each (productId, pipelineMode, authorityDimension) triple, but it does not explain how this ceiling will be validated or enforced.

allObjections.title: Over-Complexity
allObjections.detail: The introduction of three new authority sub-dimensions (Build-Authority, Deploy-Authority, Operational-Authority) may add unnecessary complexity to the system, making it more difficult to understand and manage. This could lead to errors and inconsistencies, particularly if the relationships between these sub-dimensions are not clearly defined.

allObjections.title: Complexity of Authority Dimensions
allObjections.detail: The introduction of three sub-dimensions for Authority Level (Build, Deploy, Operational) adds significant complexity. This could lead to confusion and misconfigurations, especially for operators who need to set these levels per product per mode.

allObjections.title: Lack of Prototype for Mode 2 SUB-2B
allObjections.detail: Deferring Mode 2 SUB-2B entirely from the SSOT without a prototype means that a critical part of the system remains untested and unvalidated. This could lead to integration issues when it is eventually implemented.

allObjections.title: Operational Overhead of Ownership Attestation
allObjections.detail: The requirement for operator self-attestation per URL in Mode 3B adds an operational overhead. This could slow down the process and introduce errors if operators fail to attest correctly.

allObjections.title: Ownership attestation unverifiable
allObjections.detail: Section A.1.4 operator self-attestation for URL ownership lacks technical verification mechanisms (e.g., DNS validation). This creates legal exposure where malicious operators could falsely claim ownership, triggering copyright violations during Mode 3B synthesis. The audit log records attestations but cannot prevent bad-faith submissions.

allObjections.title: JSONB ceiling storage fragility
allObjections.detail: Section A.2.4 ProductRegistry.authorityCeilings JSONB structure introduces schema drift risks. No validation constraints exist for the 4×3 matrix shape in §A.2.4 storage example. Malformed JSONB could default to recommend_only globally, breaking autonomous Mode 1 crawls unexpectedly.

allObjections.title: Degenerate config UX failure
allObjections.detail: Section B.2 validity rules reject AUTOMATIC+Supervised combos at runtime but lack user guidance. In Guided Execution Mode, an operator selecting Build=Autonomous for Mode 3B (violating B.2 rule 5) receives only API errors without inline UI corrections, worsening discoverability versus status quo console warnings.

allObjections.title: Operational-Authority crawl cost explosion
allObjections.detail: Section B.1 config #5 (Mode1/Op-Autonomous/Automatic) permits unbounded Aggressive Crawls per §6 default depth=8/pages=200. With $15/run ceiling, a product with 10 environments could incur $150/day autonomously - exceeding status quo manual crawl budgets without new budget alerts.

allObjections.title: Mode 3B remains under-specified
allObjections.detail: §A.1.4 and §D describe Mode 3B as producing a synthesized product specification, but the artifact does not define the synthesis algorithm, conflict-resolution policy, or quality bar for choosing “best elements.” That leaves the most consequential step effectively discretionary, which makes auditability and reproducibility weak even if the ownership gate is added.

allObjections.title: Authority matrix can deadlock
allObjections.detail: §A.2.4 and §B.2 create a coupled ceiling system across four modes and three authority dimensions, but the validity rules are partly contradictory: §B.2.7 says any Supervised plus Automatic is degenerate, while §B.2.8 says Automatic requires all dims Autonomous or all Recommend-only. This is brittle enough that small config changes can yield runtime rejection loops instead of predictable operator control.

allObjections.title: Self-attestation is weak evidence
allObjections.detail: §A.1.4 relies on operator self-attestation per URL for Mode 3B ownership/licensing. In real operations, this is easy to misstate accidentally or deliberately, and there is no cryptographic or third-party proof requirement, no sampling audit, and no explicit remedy for false attestations beyond runtime rejection if detected.

allObjections.title: §A.2.4 authorityCeilings JSONB novel
allObjections.detail: §A.2.4 defines ProductRegistry.authorityCeilings as 4-mode × 3-dim JSONB but §E and §F list no schema migration or AutoRunner validator; Conflict 7 admits the field does not exist today.

allObjections.title: §A.1.4 attestation lacks enforcement
allObjections.detail: Mode 3B ownershipAttestation is required at InputArtifact validation yet Conflict 8 states src/lib/renewal/inputArtifact.js has no such field and no runtime check exists.

allObjections.title: §B.2 validity rules unenforced
allObjections.detail: Eight configuration validity rules are declared but §E table shows AutoRunner POST /api/orchestrator/run still accepts any tuple; degenerate runs will reach execution before rejection.

strongest_rejection_argument.text: The strongest argument for rejecting or deferring is that the draft canonicalizes a large governance surface before the implementation evidence exists. It introduces new schema, new validation, and new authority semantics while simultaneously carving out multiple ROADMAP and FUTURE_CAPABILITIES exceptions, which suggests the spec is ahead of the product. A conservative panel could reasonably defer until the per-mode authority validator, attestation checks, and Mode 3B synthesis path are implemented and demonstrated end-to-end.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: The 3-authority-dimension model makes the system harder to operate than today's single dimension. An operator trying to enable autonomous crawling must now set 12 different ceiling values (4 modes × 3 dimensions) and risk misconfiguration that blocks legitimate runs.
adversarial.precedent: Kubernetes RBAC started with simple roles but evolved into a complex matrix of verbs × resources × namespaces that most operators misconfigure, leading to overly permissive defaults. The 3-dimension authority model risks the same fate.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The proposal should be rejected until the runtime enforcement (Conflict 10) and JSONB migration (Conflict 7) are implemented and tested. Promoting a spec with admitted implementation gaps and no rollback path for a breaking schema change violates the principle of only canonicalizing what exists. Additionally, the ownership attestation mechanism provides false security that could expose FlowAI to copyright lawsuits.

G-Q1-v2.pick_text: v2 fix resolves the overlap — ratify v2 Mode 3B definition (reports + synthesized specs only, consumed by Mode 2 SUB-2A; no parallel build pipeline) as canonical.
G-Q1-v2.rationale: Removing SUB-3B-BUILD eliminates the overlap with Mode 2, though the synthesis mechanism remains underspecified.

G-Q2-v2.pick_text: Two sub-dimensions is enough (e.g., collapse Deploy into Build or Operational).
G-Q2-v2.rationale: Deploy-Authority is redundant with Build-Authority in practice — if you can modify code, you can embed deploy logic. The 3-way split adds complexity without security benefit.

G-Q3-v2.pick_text: Per-product per-mode only — coarser; one ceiling per mode, not split by sub-dimension.
G-Q3-v2.rationale: The 4×3=12 ceiling matrix per product is too granular. Operators need per-mode control but not per-sub-dimension micromanagement.

G-Q4-v2.pick_text: v2 should ALSO defer Mode 3B (currently in SSOT as ROADMAP).
G-Q4-v2.rationale: Mode 3B's synthesis engine is completely unbuilt per §E. Like SUB-2B, it should move to FUTURE_CAPABILITIES.md until a prototype exists.

G-Q5-v2.pick_text: Attestation is right but should require third-party verification (e.g., DNS-TXT proof of ownership), not operator self-attestation.
G-Q5-v2.rationale: Self-attestation provides no legal protection. DNS-TXT or domain validation would prevent operators from falsely claiming ownership.

G-Q6-v2.pick_text: §B.2 validity rules are wrong — propose alternative.
G-Q6-v2.rationale: Rule 7 claims AUTOMATIC + Supervised is degenerate, but this could work with auto-queuing of approvals. Rule 8's constraint is arbitrary.

G-Q7-v2.pick_text: Defer to a v3 with explicit prototype implementation of the 3-sub-dimension ceiling + Mode 3B attestation before promotion.
G-Q7-v2.rationale: The proposal has too many unimplemented critical paths (JSONB migration, validity enforcement, attestation validation) to promote without working code.

perReviewer.overallNotes: The v2 proposal addresses Panel concerns in form but introduces new complexity (3-dimension authority, 12-cell ceiling matrix) without implementation backing.

G-Q3-v2.rationale: The 4×3=12 ceiling matrix per product is too granular. Operators need per-mode control but not per-sub-dimension micromanagement.

G-Q4-v2.pick_text: v2 should ALSO defer Mode 3B (currently in SSOT as ROADMAP).
G-Q4-v2.rationale: Mode 3B's synthesis engine is completely unbuilt per §E. Like SUB-2B, it should move to FUTURE_CAPABILITIES.md until a prototype exists.

G-Q5-v2.pick_text: Attestation is right but should require third-party verification (e.g., DNS-TXT proof of ownership), not operator self-attestation.
G-Q5-v2.rationale: Self-attestation provides no legal protection. DNS-TXT or domain validation would prevent operators from falsely claiming ownership.

G-Q6-v2.pick_text: §B.2 validity rules are wrong — propose alternative.
G-Q6-v2.rationale: Rule 7 claims AUTOMATIC + Supervised is degenerate, but this could work with auto-queuing of approvals. Rule 8's constraint is arbitrary.

G-Q7-v2.pick_text: Defer to a v3 with explicit prototype implementation of the 3-sub-dimension ceiling + Mode 3B attestation before promotion.
G-Q7-v2.rationale: The proposal has too many unimplemented critical paths (JSONB migration, validity enforcement, attestation validation) to promote without working code.

perReviewer.overallNotes: The v2 proposal addresses Panel concerns in form but introduces new complexity (3-dimension authority, 12-cell ceiling matrix) without implementation backing.

objections.title: Ownership attestation unverifiable
objections.detail: Section A.1.4 operator self-attestation for URL ownership lacks technical verification mechanisms (e.g., DNS validation). This creates legal exposure where malicious operators could falsely claim ownership, triggering copyright violations during Mode 3B synthesis. The audit log records attestations but cannot prevent bad-faith submissions.

objections.title: JSONB ceiling storage fragility
objections.detail: Section A.2.4 ProductRegistry.authorityCeilings JSONB structure introduces schema drift risks. No validation constraints exist for the 4×3 matrix shape in §A.2.4 storage example. Malformed JSONB could default to recommend_only globally, breaking autonomous Mode 1 crawls unexpectedly.

objections.title: Degenerate config UX failure
objections.detail: Section B.2 validity rules reject AUTOMATIC+Supervised combos at runtime but lack user guidance. In Guided Execution Mode, an operator selecting Build=Autonomous for Mode 3B (violating B.2 rule 5) receives only API errors without inline UI corrections, worsening discoverability versus status quo console warnings.

objections.title: Operational-Authority crawl cost explosion
objections.detail: Section B.1 config #5 (Mode1/Op-Autonomous/Automatic) permits unbounded Aggressive Crawls per §6 default depth=8/pages=200. With $15/run ceiling, a product with 10 environments could incur $150/day autonomously - exceeding status quo manual crawl budgets without new budget alerts.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: If an operator sets Mode 3B Operational-Authority to Autonomous while misconfiguring the ownership attestation validator (§Conflict 8), FlowAI could autonomously synthesize from competitor websites, triggering DMCA takedowns and legal liability that wouldn't occur under status quo manual research processes.
adversarial.precedent: Google Books copyright litigation (2005-2015) where automated scanning of non-licensed content resulted in protracted lawsuits, demonstrating risks of insufficient ownership verification in synthesis systems.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The three-authority-dimension model introduces untenable complexity: operators must now manage 12 independent risk ceilings per product (4 modes × 3 dims), increasing configuration errors. Combined with unverified ownership attestations in Mode 3B, this creates legal and operational risks exceeding benefits. Defer until simplified authority model and DNS-based URL verification exist.

G-Q1-v2.pick_text: v2 fix resolves the overlap — ratify v2 Mode 3B definition (reports + synthesized specs only, consumed by Mode 2 SUB-2A; no parallel build pipeline) as canonical.
G-Q1-v2.rationale: Removing SUB-3B-BUILD eliminates Mode 2/3B build duplication while preserving synthesis intent.

G-Q2-v2.pick_text: Three sub-dimensions is right but the specific naming or scope is wrong — propose adjustment.
G-Q2-v2.rationale: 'Operational-Authority' conflates crawl safety with API calls; split into 'Crawl-Authority' and 'Integration-Authority' for precision.

G-Q3-v2.pick_text: Per-product per-mode per-dimension ceiling as v2 defines — ratify (4 modes × 3 sub-dimensions = 12 independent ceilings per product).
G-Q3-v2.rationale: Per-mode granularity addresses Panel C3 by allowing different risk profiles for crawl vs. deploy actions.

G-Q4-v2.pick_text: v2 defer is correct — Mode 2 SUB-2B removed from SSOT; FUTURE_CAPABILITIES.md catalogue is the right home.
G-Q4-v2.rationale: Deferral aligns with CEO D3 and avoids overcommitting SSOT to unbuilt capabilities.

G-Q5-v2.pick_text: Attestation is right but should require third-party verification (e.g., DNS-TXT proof of ownership), not operator self-attestation.
G-Q5-v2.rationale: Self-attestation is insufficient for legal defensibility; DNS-TXT provides auditable technical proof.

G-Q6-v2.pick_text: v2 collapse is correct — ~16 canonical cells with §B.2 validity rules — ratify.
G-Q6-v2.rationale: Collapsing to non-degenerate configurations satisfies Panel C6 while excluding invalid combos like SUB-1A with Build-Autonomous.

objections.title: Mode 3B remains under-specified
objections.detail: §A.1.4 and §D describe Mode 3B as producing a synthesized product specification, but the artifact does not define the synthesis algorithm, conflict-resolution policy, or quality bar for choosing “best elements.” That leaves the most consequential step effectively discretionary, which makes auditability and reproducibility weak even if the ownership gate is added.

objections.title: Authority matrix can deadlock
objections.detail: §A.2.4 and §B.2 create a coupled ceiling system across four modes and three authority dimensions, but the validity rules are partly contradictory: §B.2.7 says any Supervised plus Automatic is degenerate, while §B.2.8 says Automatic requires all dims Autonomous or all Recommend-only. This is brittle enough that small config changes can yield runtime rejection loops instead of predictable operator control.

objections.title: Self-attestation is weak evidence
objections.detail: §A.1.4 relies on operator self-attestation per URL for Mode 3B ownership/licensing. In real operations, this is easy to misstate accidentally or deliberately, and there is no cryptographic or third-party proof requirement, no sampling audit, and no explicit remedy for false attestations beyond runtime rejection if detected.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: A team could migrate from a simpler, known-good single-ceiling model to this multi-axis system and suddenly find that common configurations are rejected as degenerate, while the accepted ones still allow ambiguous Mode 3B synthesis outputs. The result is less operationally usable governance: more false negatives at admission and less clarity about what the system is actually allowed to do.
adversarial.precedent: GitHub Copilot’s early enterprise governance discussions and several internal policy systems in large SaaS products have shown that self-attested permissions without independent verification are frequently error-prone; no precedent known for this exact three-axis SSOT structure.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The strongest argument for rejecting or deferring is that the draft canonicalizes a large governance surface before the implementation evidence exists. It introduces new schema, new validation, and new authority semantics while simultaneously carving out multiple ROADMAP and FUTURE_CAPABILITIES exceptions, which suggests the spec is ahead of the product. A conservative panel could reasonably defer until the per-mode authority validator, attestation checks, and Mode 3B synthesis path are implemented and demonstrated end-to-end.

G-Q1-v2.pick_text: v2 fix resolves the overlap — ratify v2 Mode 3B definition (reports + synthesized specs only, consumed by Mode 2 SUB-2A; no parallel build pipeline) as canonical.
G-Q1-v2.rationale: The overlap identified in v1 is explicitly removed by eliminating SUB-3B-BUILD and making Mode 3B output a spec, not a deployable build. On the text alone, that resolves the specific collision.

G-Q2-v2.pick_text: Three sub-dimensions (Build-Authority, Deploy-Authority, Operational-Authority) as v2 defines — ratify.
G-Q2-v2.rationale: The split is conceptually justified because code-writing, deployment, and runtime actions have different risk profiles and should not be forced into one knob. The naming is serviceable even if the implementation burden is high.

G-Q3-v2.pick_text: Per-product per-mode per-dimension ceiling as v2 defines — ratify (4 modes × 3 sub-dimensions = 12 independent ceilings per product).
G-Q3-v2.rationale: This is the right granularity if the system truly wants mode-specific risk control. Coarser ceilings would reintroduce the very mismatch the draft is trying to fix.

G-Q4-v2.pick_text: v2 defer is correct — Mode 2 SUB-2B removed from SSOT; FUTURE_CAPABILITIES.md catalogue is the right home.
G-Q4-v2.rationale: Removing an unbuilt capability from canonical SSOT is cleaner than labeling it roadmap inside the normative document. The future-capabilities file can track it without pretending it is operative policy.

G-Q5-v2.pick_text: Attestation is right but should require third-party verification (e.g., DNS-TXT proof of ownership), not operator self-attestation.
G-Q5-v2.rationale: Self-attestation alone is too easy to game and too weak for a governance boundary that explicitly blocks third-party synthesis. A verifiable proof mechanism would preserve the restriction while reducing abuse and accidental misrepresentation.

G-Q6-v2.pick_text: v2 collapse is correct — ~16 canonical cells with §B.2 validity rules — ratify.
G-Q6-v2.rationale: Collapsing degenerate combinations into runtime errors is preferable to bloating the SSOT with invalid states. The matrix is still complex, but at least it is now explicitly constrained.

G-Q7-v2.pick_text: v2 introduces NEW concerns not present in v1 — name them in rationale.
G-Q7-v2.rationale: The draft adds schema migration risk, unresolved implementation dependencies, and a weak ownership-attestation mechanism while also codifying a more complex governance lattice. Those are substantive new concerns, even if the conceptual direction is reasonable.

perReviewer.overallNotes: My votes accept the conceptual fixes where they close specific v1 defects, but I do not think the overall package is ready to promote unchanged because the implementation and verification story still lags the normative structure.
